sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: International Time-Definite Small Parcel Courier Operations

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, in particular Articles 101-1 et seq. on the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp); Grand-Ducal Regulation on the Register of Commerce and Companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg, under the supervision of the Ministry of Justice.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Demande d'inscription (registration request) submitted through the LBR eSpace portal, together with the acte de société (partnership agreement) or a certified extract thereof.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to the SCSp. The partnership agreement determines the value and timing of partners' contributions; no escrow account is required. In-kind contributions must be described and valued in the partnership agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED by the sole general partner of Luxembourg SCSp that: 1. The subscriptions to partnership interests listed in the subscription schedule are accepted in full. 2. The registered office is established at [address in Luxembourg], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. 3. [General Partner S.à r.l.] is appointed general partner with exclusive power to manage, represent and bind the SCSp. 4. [Name] is appointed compliance and AML officer responsible for KYC, ACH and card payment monitoring, and courier record-keeping. 5. The authorised signatories are empowered to execute the partnership agreement, file the RCS/LBR registration, obtain business and postal licences, register for VAT, and open bank accounts. 6. This resolution becomes effective upon RCS registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name verification and preliminary coordination with LBR
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RCS via the eSpace portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search request through the LBR eSpace portal using an authenticated LuxTrust electronic signature. If the requested name contains 'SCSp' or 'Special Limited Partnership', verify the corresponding entity type is available. No formal name reservation is mandatory for an SCSp, but a pre-verification avoids rejection at filing.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name including or excluding the designation 'SCSp'
Copy of the applicant's identity document
LuxTrust certificate or notary authentication evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is unavailable or rejected, submit an alternative name in a new non-refundable search request; no formal refiling penalty applies before the main registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the SCSp partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary or all partners in a private written deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the acte de société containing the identity of the general partner and limited partners, profit-sharing arrangements, management powers of the general partner, registered office in Luxembourg, and contribution schedule. Execute the deed either by private signature or before a Luxembourg notary if real property or a regulated activity requires notarisation. Ensure all partners initial every page and append a value statement for any in-kind contribution.
required_dossiers: Completed partnership agreement
Passport or national identity card of each partner
Ultimate beneficial ownership information
Consent to the registered office address
Valuation statement for in-kind contributions, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS notes ambiguity in the partnership agreement, correct the inconsistent clauses by a supplementary deed and re-execute the agreement before refiling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the completed RCS registration request in the eSpace portal, attach the executed partnership agreement, the list of managers, the registered office consent, and the UBO declaration. Use LuxTrust or a notary's online submission to authenticate the filing. Pay the applicable RCS fee. Retain the acknowledgment receipt which contains the provisional RCS number.
required_dossiers: LBR/RCS registration form
Executed partnership agreement or notarial copy
Appointment resolution of the general partner
Written consent of the registered office provider
UBO declaration and supporting identification
List of managers and powers of representation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries the application, respond within 15 calendar days through the same portal by uploading corrected annexes; no new incorporation procedure is required unless the structure itself is invalid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory publication in the RESA and issuance of the RCS extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the RCS entry is made, the partnership agreement is published electronically in RESA. Download the final RCS extract and the registration number. This extract is the authoritative formation certificate and must be used for all subsequent administrative, banking and licensing filings.
required_dossiers: Provisional or final RCS registration number
LBR filing acknowledgment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA publication contains typographical errors, file a correction request through the LBR portal; the corrected publication is dated as of the original publication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-formation licences, VAT and operating permits
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet.lu / Ministry of the Economy; Institut Luxembourgeois de Régulation (ILR) for postal/courier services; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply on Guichet.lu for the business establishment authorisation (autorisation d'établissement). For cross-border express courier services, submit the ILR postal operator authorisation or declaration. Register for VAT with the AEDT using the RCS extract and bank account details. If a warehouse or sorting facility is operated, obtain the municipal establishment permit and the environmental registration from the Environment Agency.
required_dossiers: RCS extract and partnership agreement
Business plan for the courier activity
Certificate of good conduct and professional qualification
ILR postal operator application form
AML/CFT compliance manual for payment processing
VAT registration form and bank confirmation
Warehouse site plan and environmental declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry, ILR, AEDT or municipality issues a query or refusal, cure by filing additional information within the indicated delays; administrative appeals may be lodged with the relevant minister within three months of notification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy (General Directorate for SMEs) for business establishment; Institut Luxembourgeois de Régulation (ILR) for postal/express courier authorisation; Ministère de la Mobilité et des Travaux publics for road transport aspects.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (business establishment permit) and, where applicable, autorisation d'exploitation de services postaux / express courier operator licence issued by the ILR under the Luxembourg Postal Act.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement - Environment Agency Luxembourg, under the Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / simple environmental declaration only for standard parcel sorting and delivery warehousing below the EIA thresholds; no full EIA Report required unless the facility includes fuel storage above 50 tonnes, hazardous goods storage, or large cold-storage capacity. The exact class is determined from the planned floor area and fleet size in accordance with the Law of 22 May 2008 on environmental impact assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater arises from pure courier sorting; sanitary and wash-bay wastewater must comply with municipal sewer discharge permits. Vehicle fleets must respect EU emission standards and the national air-quality plan. VOC emissions from cleaning and packaging adhesives must remain below applicable occupational thresholds under the Law on air quality and the European Industrial Emissions Directive; spill containment and waste-handling procedures must be in place for damaged parcels.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety approval from the municipal fire prevention authority and the Corps Grand-Ducal d'Incendie et de Secours (CGDIS); structural load inspection certificate by a registered engineer for mezzanine floors and racking; occupational health and safety clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM), including first-aid equipment, ventilation, and emergency evacuation plans.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; Administration des Douanes et Accises for customs and excise. Principal public portal: www.guichet.lu; e-filing portals: ACD eSpace and MyGuichet.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign SCSp operator must first complete Luxembourg RCS registration through the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) to obtain the 21-digit business registration number and the national tax identification number. For VAT, file VAT Form 640/1 (non-established taxable person) or standard Form 640 with the AEDT before carrying out taxable supplies; there is no minimum capital requirement for the SCSp. For customs/export operations, obtain an EORI number from the Administration des Douanes et Accises. Non-established operators making B2B reverse-charge supplies are generally required to register only where Luxembourg VAT is due; however, a physical express-courier branch, warehouse or regular local pickup/delivery activity creates a fixed establishment and mandates full VAT registration, invoicing and periodic returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no elective check-the-box regime. An SCSp is mandatorily fiscally transparent for direct-tax purposes: all income, gains, deductions and credits are allocated to partners in accordance with the partnership agreement. If a corporate partner is a general partner, that partner is separately subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax on its allocable share; the SCSp itself does not pay CIT. Luxembourg applies ATAD anti-hybrid election/disregard rules, which may re-characterize an SCSp that is transparent in Luxembourg but non-transparent or ignored in the partner's jurisdiction, and may deny double-deduction or deduction-without-inclusion outcomes. For VAT only, the SCSp can be registered as an independent taxable person despite lacking legal personality, and it may enter a Luxembourg VAT group under applicable conditions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée / TVA), EU VAT system
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Non-resident/non-established express courier operators: no VAT registration threshold and no de minimis; registration is due from the first Luxembourg-taxable supply. Resident/established small businesses may benefit from the EUR 35,000 annual-turnover exemption, but this exemption does not cover export/intra-EU supplies, reverse-charge services, or courier services requiring a fixed establishment; the intra-EU distance-sales threshold in Luxembourg is EUR 100,000. Express courier services physically performed in Luxembourg generally exceed any threshold because the operator has a local establishment.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API stamping, or digital seal mandate is currently in force in Luxembourg for express-courier invoicing. Taxpayers may issue electronic invoices subject to authenticity, integrity and legibility standards. Luxembourg has announced a phased Peppol-based mandatory B2B e-invoicing reform for established taxable persons, to be implemented prospectively; EDI or Peppol BIS formats must be preserved for audit. Customs exports must be filed electronically via the Union Customs Code's AES/ECS using a SAD/EX declaration, and operators must retain the LRN/export confirmation and ICS records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports to non-EU destinations qualify for 0% Luxembourg VAT where (i) title passes to the customer, (ii) the goods are physically dispatched/transported out of the EU, and (iii) the exporter holds the customs export evidence accepted by the AEDT. Express courier consignments are zero-rated when the operator is the exporter or the transport provider and a valid Union export declaration (SAD/EX) confirms exit. Ancillary transport services (freight forwarding, loading, handling, warehousing incidental to export) supplied directly in connection with third-country exports/imports are zero-rated regardless of the service provider's location if invoiced to the exporter/importer/consignee/freight forwarder. Intra-EU despatches are exempt under Article 138 EU VAT Directive if the recipient has a valid EU VAT ID and the goods are transported to another Member State; EC Sales Lists and quarterly recapitulative statements are mandatory.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Union Customs Code SAD/EX lodged in AES/ECS, with export licence/declaration and movement reference number)
Bill of Lading or Master/HAWB Air Waybill evidencing dispatch from Luxembourg and exit from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate (or equivalent SWIFT/MT103 bank credit evidence) demonstrating collection/repatriation of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT and customs authorities apply heightened scrutiny to high-volume cross-border courier zero-rating. Missing or inconsistent SAD/EX, transport or payment documentation will cause a reassessment at 17% VAT on the courier charge and/or the underlying goods, plus late-payment interest and administrative surcharges. Deliberate false customs declarations or manipulated export evidence attract criminal tax-fraud penalties including imprisonment, forfeiture and fines, as well as retrospective clawbacks up to the full VAT not collected, with the limitation periods extended in fraud cases. Failure to evidence receipt/repatriation of export proceeds within the 180-day documentary window, absent a valid commercial justification, similarly converts the zero-rating to taxable supply and triggers corrective VAT filings.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for supervised banking conduct and the Ministry of Finance for exchange-control policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible. Luxembourg applies the EU free movement of capital regime (TFEU Articles 63-66) and maintains no isolated current-account or capital-account exchange-control regime. A Luxembourg SCSp is unrestricted in receiving equity, debt, and revenue from non-resident partners, provided payments are routed through a supervised credit institution. The practical obstacles are not exchange controls but documentary proof of economic substance and of source of funds required by banks. Profit remittance to non-resident partners is legally unencumbered, with no Luxembourg withholding tax on partnership profit distributions, and only standard withholding considerations apply to Luxembourg-source interest or royalties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion requirement exists in Luxembourg. Foreign-currency courier receipts (USD, GBP, CNY) may be retained in foreign-currency accounts, switched into EUR, or used directly for outbound trade settlements at the SCSp's discretion. The only applicable obligations are standard bank anti-money-laundering verification, ECB/BCL statistical balance-of-payments reporting on cross-border payment thresholds, and corporate tax booking under Luxembourg GAAP.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte séquestre) and Operational EUR/USD Current Account
Operational Account and Corporate Cash Management; Escrow Account for Partner Capital Facilities
Multicurrency Operational Account, Call Deposits, and FX Hedging Account
Transactional Treasury Account, Foreign-Currency Working Account (USD, GBP, CNY), Trade Finance Line
Corporate SWIFT Account with ISDA/CSA Hedging Documentation
Controlled Liquidity Current Account for High-Net-Worth SCSp Structures

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility is Medium, subject to EEA passporting restrictions. An offshore digital EMI (e-money institution authorised in another EEA state) may onboard the SCSp only for payment services under PSD2; it cannot accept deposits or extend credit. Legal constraints include mandatory safeguarding of client funds, prohibition of interest-bearing operational balances, the absence of an overdraft facility, and heightened due diligence because the SCSp has no legal personality and must be contractually represented by its general partner.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg law does not categorically mandate physical presence of non-resident directors or partners for corporate account opening, and CSSF AML frameworks permit remote video identification for certain risk categories. However, for a medium-risk, enhanced-due-diligence courier SCSp, most tier-1 Luxembourg banks require at least one in-person meeting with the authorised signatory of the general partner. Remote opening is occasionally permitted through a reputable introducer, notarised and apostilled ownership documents, and a fully verified RBE transparency filing, but remains a bank-by-bank compliance decision rather than a legislative right.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unincorporated SCSp with no legal personality and opaque partnership capital structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified registration excerpt from the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), notarised partnership agreement, up-to-date RBE beneficial-ownership filing, Luxembourg legal opinion confirming existence and the general partner's binding power, full organigram of natural-person ultimate beneficial owners, and certified identity documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBOs or partners located in high-risk or non-EEA jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised passport copies of all UBOs, recent source-of-wealth reports, three years of partner bank statements, tax residence certificates, independent sanctions/PEP screening results, sworn statutory declarations on the origin of injected funds, and corporate charters of intermediate holding entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Missing or vague transport and courier licensing in Luxembourg
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg forwarding/transport permit (agrément de transporteur), Ministry of Mobility approvals, IATA cargo agent accreditation or FIAIL membership, subcontractor agreements with licensed last-mile carriers, and customs brokerage or AEO authorisation where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substance red flags such as no local premises, payroll, or operational capacity relative to declared cross-border courier activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid office lease agreement, payroll registers and Luxembourg social security (CNS/CCSS) filings, director service agreements, corporate income tax and VAT registration certificates, operational infrastructure inventory, and a substance economic dashboard showing transactional flows aligned with courier invoices.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual transaction patterns with unrelated courier counterparties, including high-volume small-amount ACH/POS settlements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master courier service contracts, commercial invoices, airway-bill manifests, customs declarations, shipment event logs, reconciliation of card settlement reports to operational systems, internal sanctions screening policy, and a documented AML/transaction-monitoring escalation protocol.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections from non-resident parents or partners must be remitted by SWIFT MT103 to the SCSp's designated Luxembourg account using the ECB/BCL balance-of-payments purpose code for Direct Investment (D) or Financial Credit (F). Documentary verification includes the capital subscription deed, partners' resolution, loan agreement where applicable, and a bank-required source-of-funds declaration. Payments above regulatory thresholds are reported monthly to the BCL for monetary and statistical purposes; no exchange-control permission is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements use a tiered clearing structure: for EEA and SEPA-zone EUR obligations, SEPA Credit Transfers (SCT) are preferred; for third-country courier and trade settlements, SWIFT MT103 (customer transfer) and MT202 (bank-to-bank) instructions are used; for high-value or supply-chain transactions, MT700 commercial letters of credit are issued with negotiating banks; customer refunds and franchise disbursements are executed through corporate cards and ACH/direct debit rails where contractually permitted. Every instruction is subject to BCL purpose-code classification, sanctions screening, and the SCSp's internal treasury approvals.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forwards (plain-vanilla, delivered) with EU-licensed bank counterparties under ISDA/CSA documentation
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs, EUR-settled) for exposures in illiquid or non-convertible franchising currencies (CNH, BDT, EGP) subject to internal bank credit limits
Cross-Currency Swaps (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP) for notional rebalancing of shareholder loans and operational debt
European-style Vanilla FX Options (buy-side only) to cap adverse currency movements without creating leveraged risk
Rolling Spot / FX Swap contracts entered exclusively with the corporate bank treasury for settlement-date liquidity smoothing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts and/or exemption declaration (déclaration de non-dépôt) filed with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) via eRegistre; publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after financial year-end; publication in RESA required once filed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-imposed fine of EUR 500 to EUR 5,000; publication of non-filing in RESA; potential judicial dissolution; manager civil liability for damages

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO annual confirmation (annual confirmation of beneficial owners)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) – Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March; any change in beneficial ownership filed within one month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to 2 years for wilful non-compliance; administrative coercion penalty of up to EUR 10,000 for late or missing confirmation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual partnership income tax return (SCSp is tax-transparent but must file for assessment of partners)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 31 December of the following calendar year; extension possible to 31 March or later on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 0.6% per month (capped at 12%); late-payment interest of 0.8% per month; ex-officio tax assessment and sanctions against the manager

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Net wealth tax declaration (applicable if the SCSp has at least one corporate partner or is otherwise liable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same deadline as the annual income tax return: by 31 December of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest (0.8% per month); monthly surcharge of 0.6% on unpaid net wealth tax; official assessment and enforcement measures

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: The SCSp must appoint an independent statutory auditor (‘réviseur d’entreprises agréé’) if it exceeds two of the three following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million; net turnover EUR 8.8 million; average headcount 50. A partner holding at least 20% of voting rights may also trigger a mandatory audit request.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (plan comptable luxembourgeois) for statutory annual accounts; IFRS as adopted by the EU is optionally permitted for consolidated or voluntary accounts; SCSp remains tax-transparent and accounts are prepared for commercial parity and distribution tracking.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must identify all beneficial owners and file their data with the RBE. An annual confirmation covering all registered UBO records is due every year by 31 March. Any transfer of partnership interests (shares of partnership capital) must be documented in a formal deed or decision, reflected in the internal register of partners, and reported to the RBE within one month. The manager remains responsible for ensuring the register is complete and accurate.
